text:
maya-ops: FYI customer reported their GCP marketplace invoice shows ~3x the tokens we show in Redwood dashboard for project redwood-cust-301. invoice: INV-GCP-9923, attached screenshot.

samir-billing: ugh. any chance this is the usual timezone/aggregation lag? what's the delta in absolute tokens?

maya-ops: customer says GCP line items have 12,450,000 tokens but our billing dashboard shows 4,120,432 tokens for the same billing period (2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28). they sent the marketplace csv, looks like GCP combined two product SKUs into one line: "Redwood Inference - processed_units" + "Redwood Inference - embeddings" collapsed.

liam-infra: can you paste the raw line item rows? or attach the CSV. possible tag mismatch between our metering product_code and the marketplace product_id.

maya-ops: pasted the two suspicious rows from csv: `product_id: redwood.meter.v1, usage_amount: 8245432, unit: tokens` and `product_id: redwood.embeddings.v1, usage_amount: 4200000, unit: tokens` -> GCP UI shows a single line 12445432 tokens. customer thinks they were double-charged because earlier we bill embeddings and generation separately but GCP rolled them up.

samir-billing: thanks. two hypotheses: 1) our metering reported both SKUs and GCP aggregated them into one line but customer is missing our internal dedupe (we dedupe overlapping calls). 2) meter id mapping changed when customer migrated project id -> old usage reattributed. need to confirm whether our metering pipeline emitted overlapping events for those timestamps.

billing-bot: Automated report for INV-GCP-9923: matched_redwood_usage=4,120,432 tokens; marketplace_reported=12,445,432 tokens; unmatched=8,325,000 tokens. export available: https://storage.redwood/internal/recon/INV-GCP-9923.csv

jess-finance: tagging @samir-billing @liam-infra — if unmatched tokens > 1M we should consider issuing a provisional credit while we investigate. customers escalate fast on marketplace billing.

liam-infra: agreed. steps I'll run: 1) check metering event stream for project redwood-cust-301 for 2026-02-01..28: `gsutil cp gs://redwood-metering/export/redwood-cust-301/2026-02/*.ndjson .` then `jq -r '. | select(.meter=="redwood.meter.v1" or .meter=="redwood.embeddings.v1") | .timestamp + " 	" + (.tokens|tostring)'` to check overlap. will also diff against the GCP csv.

maya-ops: customer asked for repro steps they can run on their side to convince internal procurement: they can export marketplace usage report and match on `usage_start_time` + `product_id`. sending example query they can run in BigQuery: `SELECT product_id, SUM(usage_amount) FROM marketplace_usage WHERE invoice_id="INV-GCP-9923" GROUP BY product_id;`

samir-billing: we should also surface whether we dedupe by request_id or by client_request_id. if GCP collapsed server-side, they may not preserve request ids. @liam-infra can you check if our events contain a common client_id that would cause double counting once aggregated by GCP?

liam-infra: on it. quick note: I see in the meter stream some events missing `client_request_id` for one of the SKUs around 2026-02-14 03:00 UTC — suspect ingestion retry created duplicate tokens with new request ids. will confirm counts shortly.

maya-ops: I've asked the customer to confirm whether they created any project migrations in mid-Feb. they said yes (moved to new billing account on 2026-02-13) — that timing matches the spike.

jess-finance: provisional plan: if infra confirms ingestion duplicates tied to migration we issue a one-time credit equal to unmatched tokens * unit_price. please prepare a draft credit note.

samir-billing: also opening a HC ticket with GCP marketplace support (ref: REDWOOD-ISSUE-7621) to ask them for the line-item attribution rules when multiple product_ids map to the same marketplace product. include CSV and our computed diff.

billing-bot: Ticket created: GCP-12345678. SLA: 5 business days. Link: https://console.gcp/support/tickets/GCP-12345678

liam-infra: initial numbers: our ndjson dump shows total tokens for the two meters = 12,445,432 (matches marketplace) but after applying our dedupe by client_request_id it's 4,120,432. so GCP aggregated raw events (including retries) and charged total raw tokens — we dedupe server-side later.

maya-ops: that's the smoking gun. customer needs to be credited for the duplicates. jess, how fast can we issue provisional credit?

jess-finance: I can draft and issue a credit today once we have final unmatched token delta and confirm pricing tier. will need approval from legal for marketplace adjustment.

samir-billing: action items: liam to produce proof-of-dedupe script and final numbers (ETA 2h). maya to coordinate credit note with customer and collect proof of project migration. jess to prepare credit draft. I'll keep the GCP ticket warm.

maya-ops: thanks team, I'll update the customer and leave a note in the support case. :thumbsup:
